jobs.title: Assistant General Counsel - M&A Global Investment Banking - Vice President
jobs.description:
The Global Investment Banking Legal Practice Group provides legal support to the firm’s Capital Markets, M&A Advisory and Research groups.  Among other topics, this Practice Group provides primary legal coverage to the Mergers and Acquisitions teams on M&A laws and related matters, including drafting, reviewing and negotiating on a full range of documentation (such as engagement letters, fairness opinions, valuation letters, transactional proxy disclosures and confidentiality agreements). The Practice Group supports many of the firm’s most innovative and cutting edge transactions and initiatives and is significantly involved in shaping industry views on market practice developments. This is an excellent opportunity for a junior/mid-level attorney with a strong foundation in M&A transactions to join a successful, well-established global team of professionals and be a part of one of the premier investment banks in the country and the world.

As a Vice President, Assistant General Counsel in the Global Investment Banking Legal Practice Group you will focus on the firm’s M&A transactional work, including public and private sell side, buy side, strategic, and defense transactions.  The attorney in this role will handle reviewing, drafting, negotiating and advising on the full range of documentation relating to M&A transactions (e.g., engagement letters, fairness opinions, valuation letters, transactional proxy disclosures and NDAs). Additionally, the attorney will advise on a wide variety of related legal, conflicts and litigation risk mitigation issues. You will work both independently and with colleagues across the Practice Group (Capital Markets and Research) and across the Firm, including Compliance, Conflicts and Litigation, and will also manage and supervise external counsel engaged in related assignments.

The Legal Department at JPMorgan Chase & Co. manages legal and other risks, advises on products and services, interprets laws and regulations that impact the firm, and advises the firm on other matters.  Our global team is made up of about 2,000 lawyers and legal professionals with a reputation as thought leaders who deliver best-in-class services. As trusted advisors, we help the firm’s clients while also safeguarding the integrity of the firm.  We are committed to a culture of inclusivity and belonging, where people can grow and succeed throughout their careers while working for a first-in-class financial institution doing cutting-edge work. If these values resonate with you, we would like to hear from you.

Job responsibilities

- Draft and / or negotiate engagement letters, indemnity letters, NDAs, etc.

- Review of fairness opinions, valuation presentations, merger agreements, M&A related proxy statements and registration statements and other M&A transaction agreements.

- Provide guidance and subject matter expertise on new and existing legal and/ or regulatory requirements to internal business and functional partners, including Compliance, Conflicts and Litigation.

- Partner with senior attorneys to assist with training and other department initiatives.

- Manage and update template documents, such as contracts, guidelines, memos and other documents.

- Contribute to the development of industry positions on market developments.

Required qualifications, capabilities and skills

- Law school degree (JD) and admission to NY bar required.

- Extensive experience reviewing, drafting and / or negotiating M&A transaction documents, e.g. engagement letters, merger agreements, fairness opinions, valuation presentations, proxy statements, registration statements, NDAs and other documents relating to public and private M&A transactions.

- Excellent drafting skills, strong attention to detail and ability to work independently on transactions and projects.

- Strong analytical, problem-solving and legal research skills. Proven ability to independently identify issues, analyze problems and provide viable solutions.

- Enthusiastic, “can-do” attitude is critical to role, as well as a strong desire to work closely with M&A bankers and the Legal practice group.

- Polished verbal and written communication skills; ability to effectively communicate complex legal issues to senior managers or executives and to negotiate with clients.

- Team player, confident and proactive, with strong interpersonal skills and ability to build consensus across a global matrix organization.

- Ability to work accurately under pressure, handle deadlines, and manage multiple tasks in a high performance environment.

Preferred qualifications, capabilities and skills

- Minimum of five full years’ experience, including M&A transactional background, contract drafting and negotiation work.   Prior experience working for or representing a full service investment bank (on M&A, Capital Markets or other transactional assignments) is a strong plus.

- Familiarity with landmark Delaware case law related to M&A litigation. Conflicts management familiarity a strong plus.

- Strong interest in new and emerging technology solutions and applications, including a baseline understanding of AI concepts, and issues relative to such technologies.

All candidates for roles in the Legal department must successfully complete a conflicts of interest clearance review prior to commencement of employment. Attorneys must be licensed to practice law and a member in good standing or otherwise eligible to practice law in the jurisdiction in which the position is based.

As a Quantitative Portfolio Manager, VP, within Wealth Management’s Chief Investment Office (CIO) – Equities team, you will be a senior leader in a growing, innovative Equity Portfolio Management organization, reporting to the Head of Equities. You will set the quantitative research agenda, own core portfolio analytics and risk frameworks, and drive implementation of systematic, factor-based and data-driven insights for an $80bn equity portfolio benchmarked against MSCI World.

This role requires deep expertise in equity factor research, portfolio construction, and risk management—combined with the credibility to influence other senior portfolio managers and fundamental analysts. You will translate complex quantitative work into investment decisions, elevate the team’s analytical capabilities, and serve as a thought partner to CIO leadership on process, tooling, governance, and portfolio outcomes.

Responsibilities

- Quantitative leadership & investment partnership

- Act as the senior quantitative partner to the equity team, influencing security selection overlays, factor tilts, risk budgeting, and implementation choices across regional and global mandates.

- Lead the integration of quantitative signals with fundamental views, ensuring a repeatable, well-governed investment process.

- Risk model ownership & portfolio risk governance

- Own the application and interpretation of multi-factor risk models (e.g., Axioma and/or equivalent) to monitor exposures, crowding, concentration, liquidity considerations, and scenario sensitivities.

- Establish escalation frameworks and decision support for material risks; contribute to portfolio review cadence and senior risk discussions.

- Portfolio construction, optimization & attribution

- Design and improve portfolio construction frameworks including constraints, turnover control, transaction cost awareness, and rebalancing discipline.

- Lead performance attribution and factor decomposition to diagnose drivers of returns, active risk, and drawdowns; turn findings into actionable portfolio recommendations.

- Data, engineering & advanced analytics

- Drive development of scalable research and analytics tooling (Python-first), including data pipelines, reusable libraries, and standardized reporting for PM workflows.

- Evaluate and apply machine learning/AI techniques where appropriate (feature engineering, ensemble methods, NLP for alternative data), with emphasis on interpretability and investment relevance.

- Stakeholder management & communication

- Communicate complex quantitative concepts clearly to senior investment professionals; deliver crisp trade-offs and recommendations rather than “model outputs.”

- Partner with technology, data, risk, compliance, and control stakeholders to ensure model governance and appropriate use.

- Controls & compliance

-
Maintain a consistent focus on risk management, model governance, suitability, and adherence to applicable policies and controls.

Required Responsibilities, Capabilities and Skills:

- 6+ years of experience in quantitative investing, equity research, portfolio construction, or risk analytics (buy-side preferred), with demonstrated impact on portfolio outcomes (alpha, risk-adjusted returns, drawdown control, implementation efficiency).

- Deep understanding of equity markets, factor investing, risk modeling, and portfolio construction under real-world constraints (turnover, costs, liquidity, client guidelines).

- Proven experience owning or heavily influencing risk model usage (Axioma or similar), exposure management, scenario analysis, and attribution.

- Advanced programming capability in Python, including strong applied experience with data analysis libraries (Pandas, NumPy, SciPy, stats/ML stack) and production-quality research practices (version control, testing, code review).

- Solid grounding in statistics/econometrics and familiarity with ML techniques appropriate for investment contexts (regularization, tree-based methods, cross-validation, time-series pitfalls).

-
Bachelor’s degree required;

jobs.title: Private Equity  - Fund Administration - Associate
jobs.description:
J.P. Morgan Alternative Fund Services (“AFS”) is part of the Securities Services business group in the Corporate & Investment Bank and is one of the largest fund and portfolio administration businesses in the industry, administering over $950 billion in assets globally. The business was launched in November 2005 through the commercialization of the finance and technology teams supporting J.P. Morgan's various private equity and real estate entities. Our AFS business has over 950 dedicated professionals with offices in Dublin, London, Luxembourg, New York, New Jersey, Bangalore, Guernsey, Hong Kong, Jersey, Singapore, Toronto, and Sydney. We provide administration services to more than 150 clients across all alternative asset classes.

As a Private Equity Fund Admin Associate within our client administration team, you will support the management of daily client deliverables for Private Equity fund administration clients. Your responsibilities will include assisting with the upkeep of books and records, computation of Net Asset Valuations, preparation of financial statements, overseeing capital events, calculating management fees and carried interest, allocating investor capital and statements, releasing investor reports, and coordinating the year-end process with audit and tax teams. You will also assist in managing client expectations and deliverable timelines in line with SLAs, and ensuring prompt resolution of client issues and escalations. Your role will require a solid understanding of Private Equity fund structures, proficiency in accounting for complex transactions, and a comprehensive knowledge of fund governing documents.

Job Responsibilities:

- Support all aspects of client deliverables for Private Equity fund administration clients including client expectations and timelines as well as any issues and escalations.

- Stay abreast of industry standards and best practices while continuously seeking opportunities to enhance operational efficiency and mitigate operational risks.

- Liaise with support functions and internal stakeholders including risk and control groups, audit, compliance, implementation, investor relations, and operations.

- Ensure adherence to control framework including prescribed policies and procedures.

- Assist in ad hoc client projects and internal initiatives.

- Collaborate with team members and contribute to staff development while providing oversight and supervision on technical topics and client-related issues.

- Review fund governing documents, side letters, and agreements to determine impact on reporting deliverables and ensure adherence.

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills:

- A professional accounting qualification (CA, CPA) combined with 4+ years of experience working with Private Equity funds in a fund administration or related capacity.

- Knowledge of US GAAP for Investment Funds and a thorough understanding of Private Equity fund structures.

- Bachelor’s Degree in Accounting, Finance, or MBA.

- Ability to work under pressure to meet tight deadlines and balance multiple priorities.

- Strong attention to detail and a collaborative management style.

- Team player with excellent problem-solving, communication, and client service skills as well as the ability to take ownership and manage projects.

- Proficiency in Microsoft Office product suite and advanced MS Excel skills.

Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills:

- Strong knowledge of Investran or similar integrated Private Equity system a plus.

- Investment fund audit experience with a Big 4 firm a plus.

jobs.title: Investment Banking - Private Capital Advisory, GP-Led Secondaries - Analyst
jobs.description:
We are seeking a highly motivated Analyst to join the Secondary Advisory team of Private Capital Advisory & Solutions, with a focus on GP-led secondary transactions. The team advises private equity sponsors and other alternative asset managers on liquidity and capital solutions across the private-fund lifecycle. Transactions may include single-asset and multi-asset continuation vehicles, preferred equity solutions, and other structured secondary transactions. The Analyst will work closely with senior bankers, financial sponsors, portfolio-company management teams, secondary investors, limited partners, legal counsel, and other transaction advisers. The role provides significant exposure to transaction structuring, financial analysis, valuation, marketing, and end-to-end execution within the growing private-capital secondary market. The Analyst will work in a collaborative, apprenticeship-oriented environment with meaningful responsibility and direct interaction with senior members of the team.

Job Responsibilities

- Support the origination and execution of GP-led secondary transactions, including single-asset and multi-asset continuation vehicles

- Build and maintain financial models, including operating models, valuation analyses, leveraged-buyout models, investor-return analyses, and continuation-vehicle capitalization models

- Prepare presentations, pitch books, confidential information memoranda, management presentations, investor materials, process letters, and internal approval materials

- Coordinate with industry coverage teams, M&A professionals, capital-markets teams, legal counsel, tax advisers, accounting firms, and other transaction participants

- Assist in the preparation and management of virtual data rooms and coordinate due-diligence requests across clients, management teams, investors, and advisers

- Support outreach to prospective secondary investors and maintain buyer lists, outreach logs, process trackers, and bid-comparison materials

- Monitor GP-led secondary-market activity, investor appetite, fundraising trends, pricing dynamics, and relevant precedent transactions

- Maintain internal databases covering secondary investors, transaction precedents, market activity, and sponsor relationships

- Support senior bankers in client meetings, business-development initiatives, and strategic discussions with financial sponsors

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills

- Bachelor’s degree with a strong academic record

- Up to three years of relevant experience in investment banking, private capital advisory, private equity, secondary investing, transaction advisory, valuation, or a related field

- Excellent quantitative and analytical skills  with a strong understanding of financial statements, accounting principles, corporate finance, and valuation methodologies

- Strong written and verbal communication skills.

- Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to producing accurate, high-quality work

- Organizational skills with an ability to manage multiple assignments and work effectively in a fast-paced, transaction-oriented environment

- Strong judgment, integrity, professionalism, and discretion

- Demonstrated interest in private equity, private markets, and secondary transactions

Preferred Qualifications

- Familiarity with GP-led secondaries, continuation vehicles, or private-fund structures

- Experience with leveraged-buyout modeling, private-equity transactions, or sponsor coverage

- Understanding of private-equity fund economics, including management fees, carried interest, fund waterfalls and limited-partner elections

- Knowledge of secondary investors, financial sponsors, and institutional limited partners

This role encompasses the performance of regulated activity. The successful candidate will therefore be subject to meeting certain regulatory requirements.


We are seeking a highly motivated Analyst to join the Secondary Advisory team of Private Capital Advisory & Solutions, with a focus on GP-led secondary transactions.

We are seeking a highly motivated Associate to join the Secondary Advisory team of Private Capital Advisory & Solutions, with a focus on GP-led secondary transactions. The team advises private equity sponsors and other alternative asset managers on liquidity and capital solutions across the private-fund lifecycle. Transactions may include single-asset and multi-asset continuation vehicles, preferred equity solutions, and other structured secondary transactions. The Associate will work closely with senior bankers, financial sponsors, portfolio-company management teams, secondary investors, limited partners, legal counsel, and other transaction advisers. The role provides significant exposure to transaction structuring, financial analysis, valuation, marketing, and end-to-end execution within the growing private-capital secondary market. The Associate will work in a collaborative, apprenticeship-oriented environment with meaningful responsibility and direct interaction with senior members of the team, including leading key workstreams and guiding junior team members.

Job Responsibilities

- Support and drive the origination and execution of GP-led secondary transactions, including single-asset and multi-asset continuation vehicles

- Own core analytical workstreams and oversee day-to-day modeling and valuation efforts, including operating models, valuation analyses, LBO models, investor return analyses, and continuation vehicle capitalization models

- Review and refine presentations, pitch books, confidential information memoranda, management presentations, investor materials, process letters, and internal approval materials

- Coordinate and manage workstreams across industry coverage teams, M&A professionals, capital-markets teams, legal counsel, tax advisers, accounting firms, and other transaction participants

- Help run the diligence process, including preparation and management of virtual data rooms and coordination of due-diligence requests across clients, management teams, investors, and advisers

- Support investor outreach and process management, including maintaining buyer lists, outreach logs, process trackers, and bid-comparison materials; assist in managing timelines and communications across parties

- Monitor and synthesize GP-led secondary-market activity, investor appetite, fundraising trends, pricing dynamics, and relevant precedent transactions to inform client advice and positioning

- Maintain and enhance internal databases covering secondary investors, transaction precedents, market activity, and sponsor relationships

- Support senior bankers in client meetings, business-development initiatives, and strategic discussions with financial sponsors; contribute to meeting preparation and follow-up materials

- Coach and develop Analysts, including providing guidance on modeling, materials preparation, and execution best practices (as applicable)

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills

- Bachelor’s degree with a strong academic record

- 3–5 years of relevant experience in investment banking, private capital advisory, private equity, secondary investing, transaction advisory, valuation, or a related field

- Excellent quantitative and analytical skills with a strong understanding of financial statements, accounting principles, corporate finance, and valuation methodologies

- Strong written and verbal communication skills

- Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to producing accurate, high-quality work

- Organizational skills with an ability to manage multiple assignments and work effectively in a fast-paced, transaction-oriented environment

- Strong judgment, integrity, professionalism, and discretion

- Demonstrated interest in private equity, private markets, and secondary transactions

Preferred Qualifications

- Familiarity with GP-led secondaries, continuation vehicles, or private-fund structures

- Experience with leveraged-buyout modeling, private-equity transactions, or sponsor coverage

- Understanding of private-equity fund economics, including management fees, carried interest, fund waterfalls, and limited-partner elections

- Knowledge of secondary investors, financial sponsors, and institutional limited partners

- Experience reviewing junior work product and managing discrete workstreams (preferred)

This role encompasses the performance of regulated activity. The successful candidate will therefore be subject to meeting certain regulatory requirements.


We are seeking a highly motivated Associate to join the Secondary Advisory team of Private Capital Advisory & Solutions, with a focus on GP-led secondary transactions.

jobs.title: Payments Corporate Development and Partnerships-Vice President
jobs.description:
Opportunity to shape the future of payments and commerce by driving transformational partnerships and investments

As a Vice President in Corporate Development and Partnerships, You will identify and execute strategic partnerships—and, where applicable, investment opportunities—that accelerate product innovation and commercial growth across our global payments and commerce capabilities. This role sits at the intersection of client needs, product strategy, and external ecosystem development, working closely with Product, Sales, Technology, Legal, Risk, and Investments.

Job responsibilities:

- Source and evaluate partnership opportunities that differentiate J.P. Morgan Payments and drive measurable client and business outcomes.

- Build strategic business cases including value proposition, target clients/use cases, competitive landscape, economics, and execution roadmap.

- Lead partner engagement end-to-end, including outreach, qualification, negotiation of commercial terms, and internal alignment through approvals.

- Drive commercialization and go-to-market, coordinating with Sales and Marketing on positioning, enablement, pipeline creation, and client adoption.

- Coordinate cross-functional execution across Product, Sales, Technology, Legal, Compliance/Risk, Operations, and Investments to deliver launches on schedule.

- Conduct diligence for investment and partnership decisions, assessing strategic fit, product/technology, financials, risks, and integration considerations.

- Develop and maintain ecosystem relationships with fintechs, venture capital, incubators, and industry forums to keep a strong pipeline of opportunities.

Required qualifications, capabilities and skills:

- 7+ years of relevant experience in corporate development, strategy, product partnerships, and/or payments/fintech-related roles.

- Demonstrated ability to synthesize market, client, and product signals into clear recommendations and actionable partnership strategies.

- Strong structured communication skills (written and verbal), with the ability to influence stakeholders from working teams through senior leadership.

- Proven negotiation and deal execution capability, including commercial structuring and stakeholder alignment.

- Strong program and stakeholder management skills, effectively driving multiple concurrent workstreams to outcomes.

-
A collaborative, ownership-oriented approach, with comfort operating in ambiguity and translating strategy into execution.

Preferred qualifications, capabilities and skills:

- Experience building and commercializing payments and/or commerce solutions through external partners.

- Strong understanding of enterprise payments needs (e.g., pay-ins, pay-outs, treasury flows, acceptance, ERP integrations, reconciliation).

- Background in product partnerships, corporate development, strategy, or fintech business development, including operating within complex, regulated environments.

- Experience with investment evaluation (strategic or financial), including diligence and investment committee materials.

- Exposure to international payments markets and cross-border partnership execution; Familiarity with emerging technologies and human-centered/design-led product discovery approaches.

- Familiarity with emerging technologies and human-centered/design-led product discovery approaches.


Opportunity to shape the future of payments and commerce by driving transformational partnerships and investments

jobs.title: 2027 Global Corporate Banking Analyst Program - Summer Internship - London
jobs.description:
As a 2027 Global Corporate Banking Summer Intern, you will start with an orientation and training led by our top professionals and expert instructors which will arm you with the technical and practical knowledge you'll need to make your mark in Global Corporate Banking. Our team members and mentors will help you navigate the firm and continue to learn about our businesses. Access to senior management and a strong network of peers will promote ongoing professional development throughout the summer. Top performing summer analysts may receive a full-time offer to join the two-year Global Corporate Banking analyst program.

You’ll join one of several specialised teams within Global Corporate Banking.

- Mid-Cap Team: Provides tailored corporate and investment banking solutions to multinational mid-cap companies, leveraging industry expertise and in-depth financial analysis to support clients’ day-to-day and strategic needs.

- Infrastructure Team: Covers leading global infrastructure fund investors across sectors such as digital, energy, transportation, and social infrastructure, offering significant exposure to senior bankers and cross-functional collaboration.

- Subsidiary Team: Delivers integrated banking services to EMEA subsidiaries of multinational clients, with a focus on understanding regional operations and supporting industry- and geography-specific needs.

- Innovation Economy Team: Supports high-growth, VC- and PE-backed technology and life sciences companies with global banking, venture lending, and strategic advisory, emphasizing long-term partnerships and sector expertise.

Job Responsibilities

- Assisting GCB bankers in managing internal aspects of existing client relationships

- Helping with industry and credit analysis, including reviewing financial statements, supporting the credit approval and documentation process

- Gaining exposure to product, strategy, or client coverage-based teams

- Preparing internal memos, for example senior management briefings, decision committee memoranda

- Participating in the analysis and negotiation of financing requests in coordination with credit, product, legal and compliance teams

- Coordinating with product and country teams to identify and execute transactions for clients globally across a range of products, for example capital markets, risk solutions, transaction banking

- Networking with industry leaders, accessing best-in-class training and learning how all our businesses work together to provide excellent customer service

.  Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills

- Familiarity with business fundamentals

- Ability to quickly solve problems on your own and with a team

- Enthusiasm, energy and a drive to succeed

- A collaborative mindset and willingness to partner and work on a team

- The confidence and initiative to take on early responsibility and manage your own projects

- Proficiency in MS Word and Excel

- Fluency in English

- Expected graduation dates January 2028 - August 2028

Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills

- Being on-track for a United Kingdom 2:1 Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) in your undergraduate studies.

Application deadline: 1st November 2026

We will be filling our classes on a rolling basis. We strongly encourage you to submit your application as early as possible before job postings close.

jobs.title: Global AV & Collaboration Technology Operations Lead
jobs.description:
Join us as the Global AV & Collaboration Technology Operations Lead and help shape how teams connect and collaborate across the globe. You will drive operational excellence, champion innovation, and foster a secure, reliable collaboration technology environment. This is your opportunity to lead a diverse, globally distributed team, influence strategic direction, and promote a culture of continuous improvement. At JPMorganChase, you can make a lasting impact while advancing your career.

As a Global AV & Collaboration Technology Operations Lead in Workplace Services Operations, you will own the global service operations model for the firm’s enterprise audio-visual (AV), video conferencing, unified communications (UC), and collaboration space estate. You will oversee meeting rooms, conference and huddle spaces, event venues, digital signage, and room technology across our global office portfolio. You will lead regional operations and vendor teams, ensuring global consistency in support standards and controls. You will manage SLAs, escalations, and financial planning, partnering with product and engineering teams to ensure every new platform is supportable from day one. This role focuses on enterprise workplace technology, not media production or creative content.

Job Responsibilities:
- Own the global service operations model for enterprise AV, conferencing, UC, and collaboration spaces, ensuring consistent support standards and controls across all regions
- Define, manage, and report against Service Level Agreements (SLAs) and operational KPIs for collaboration spaces and AV services
- Oversee global incident, problem, and escalation management for AV and conferencing services, including major incident response and root-cause analysis
- Ensure readiness and support for high-visibility events, town halls, and executive meetings
- Manage global and regional AV managed-service, field-service, and integration vendors, including performance reviews and remediation plans
- Oversee vendor resourcing models, coverage, and escalation paths
- Partner with Sourcing and Third-Party Oversight on contracts, renewals, and vendor risk requirements
- Manage global financials, including operating expenses, accruals, and forecasting
- Drive a robust risk and controls framework, leading the team through audits and regulatory reviews
- Partner with product and engineering teams for early engagement on new platforms and hardware standards
- Develop internal tooling strategies, prioritizing efficiency, automation, and controls

Required Qualifications, Capabilities, and Skills:
- Experience leading or supporting service operations within enterprise AV, conferencing, UC, or collaboration technology environments
- Demonstrated experience in operations management across vendor, field service, ticket, and asset/media management operations at a global or multi-region scale
- Proven ownership of SLA definition and management, incident and escalation management, and service performance reporting
- Strong vendor management experience, including managed-service or field-service providers and third-party performance governance
- Working knowledge of enterprise AV and collaboration technology, including video conferencing platforms and room systems (e.g., Zoom Rooms, Microsoft Teams Rooms, Cisco/Webex), AV signal distribution, audio DSP, displays, and related infrastructure
- Experience operating within a risk and controls environment, including audit preparation and evidence management
- Expertise in process and tool innovation to enhance operational efficiency
- Strong leadership and organizational skills with the ability to drive change across a distributed team
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills with a customer-centric approach, including comfort engaging senior stakeholders
- Ability to collaborate with global peers and manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment
- Understanding of AI and automation to innovate solutions that positively impact cost, risk, and customer satisfaction

Preferred Qualifications, Capabilities, and Skills:
- Experience supporting AV and collaboration services in a large corporate, financial services, or other regulated environment
- Familiarity with ITIL service management practices
- Experience with AV/room monitoring and analytics platforms and ITSM toolsets (e.g., ServiceNow)
- Industry certifications such as CTS, or vendor certifications across major conferencing platforms

Why Join Us?
You will be part of a global team that values innovation, collaboration, and continuous improvement. We offer opportunities for career growth, a supportive environment, and the chance to make a meaningful impact on how our teams connect and succeed.

jobs.title: Control Manager - Program - Controls Room – Program Management Vice President
jobs.description:
Help shape how Control Management delivers consistent, high-quality outcomes through modern data, design, and intelligent tooling. In this role, you will lead program execution across product and technology partners while keeping governance routines, roadmaps, and releases moving forward. You will turn priorities into clear plans, milestones, and transparent reporting that enables informed decisions. You will build strong partnerships across technology, data, and control stakeholders to deliver a cohesive experience and measurable results.
As a Vice President, Program Management in the Controls Room team within Control Management, you coordinate product and technology initiatives and translate priorities into clear delivery plans, governance routines, and senior stakeholder reporting. You will work with us to ensure roadmaps, milestones, dependencies, and release activities are well-defined and executed in a fast-paced, evolving environment. You will partner across product owners, data science, reporting, technology teams, and control stakeholders to strengthen alignment and transparency. We value thoughtful collaboration, clear communication, and disciplined execution as we deliver intelligent tooling and technology outcomes.
Job responsibilities
- Lead coordination across product and technology workstreams, ensuring deliverables, milestones, and dependencies are defined, tracked, and executed.
- Lead alignment across business, product, technology, and risk/control stakeholders to resolve cross-program dependencies and remove execution barriers.
- Execute program routines that translate priorities into actionable plans, integrated roadmaps, governance cadences, and measurable outcomes.
- Facilitate workshops and intake forums to assess change requests, confirm impacts, and align priorities to the roadmap.
- Manage program scorecards and milestone tracking, including alignment across product-owned processes and the broader program scorecard.
- Coordinate release planning and release readiness routines, including milestone management, stakeholder coordination, and execution reporting.
- Coordinate data migration planning and production go-live activities, including readiness checkpoints, issue resolution, and post-implementation follow-up.

jobs.title: Chase Auto Vehicle Remarketing Business Operations Manager I - Associate
jobs.description:
Do you like engaging with internal and external stakeholders in a high impact role within an exciting business?  We are looking for an Asset Remarketing Operations Manager to join our team.

As the Vehicle Remarketing Asset Remarketing  Business Operations Manager in Vehicle Remarketing Operations, you will oversee vehicle titling functions supporting the Asset Remarketing vehicle sale process. These functions include internal title collection, determination of negotiability, external application for negotiable title, distribution of title for sale or account closure activities, vendor oversight, performance monitoring, and rate control. Timely execution of these processes will facilitate prompt vehicle sale scheduling and minimizing days in inventory.

Job Responsibilities

• Oversee Title support staff assuring adherence to procedures, established service standards, and Bank policy.

• Administer performance management review and discussions with team

• Monitor title process to assure all activities are executed timely. • Identify and engage in situations delaying title application to assure/determine the best method of resolution is used.

• Monitor process flows to identify opportunities to add efficiency, document recommendations, update procedures, and implement approved solutions.

• Assure the generation and distribution of daily, weekly, and monthly operational reporting. Validate performance reporting and prepare monthly scorecard summary.

• Reviewing and authorizing payment of title service invoices and relevant bills received

• Strong verbal and written communication skills

• Strong negotiation, analytical, problem resolution, and decision making skills

• Strong ability to analyze department reporting to identify process gaps and opportunities and offer solutions to existing or potential problems

• Strong ability to effectively utilize business tools including Word, Excel, Teams, etc.

• Strong ability to identify enhancements to existing performance reporting and develop new reporting as needed to measure process efficiency.

Preferred Qualifications, Capabilities, and Skills

• Bachelor’s degree or 3+ years supervisory/leadership experience

• 3+ years experience in the vehicle remarketing industry supporting remarketing related activities

• 5+ years experience dealing with all aspects of title processing on a national basis


Oversee vehicle titling functions supporting the Asset Remarketing vehicle sale process

jobs.title: Lead Solutions Analyst - Cloud Business Operations
jobs.description:
Lead the forefront of innovative solutions analysis in a dynamic tech environment, driving success through expertise in data analytics and technical program delivery.

As a Lead Solutions Analyst  within  the JPMorganChase Cloud Business Operations team, you will play a central role in driving the success of our technical program delivery. Your deep understanding of applications, platforms, and products will position you as a key bridge between product owners, business, operations, and software developers. Utilizing advanced analytical reasoning and technical fluency, you will translate complex business requirements into well-structured and technically feasible solutions. You will make data-informed decisions and provide strategic insights to support key business initiatives. As a technical subject matter expert, you'll navigate ambiguity, manage change effectively, and communicate compellingly with diverse stakeholder audiences to ensure the highest quality and professionalism in service delivery.

Cloud Business Operations team and is responsible for end-to-end financial management of public cloud spend, including cost allocation, monthly billing execution, and analysis of month-over-month spend drivers. Job Responsibilities

- Lead the elicitation, documentation, and validation of business and data flow requirements, ensuring alignment with stakeholder expectations and technical feasibility

- Uses enterprise-authorized AI capabilities within the work environment to accelerate requirements synthesis and solution optioning, validating outputs and handling data according to sensitivity and security requirements.

- Model the design and implementation of technical solutions, ensuring seamless integration with existing systems and infrastructure

- Utilize advanced data analytics techniques to extract insights from large, diverse datasets, driving data-informed decision-making and supporting key business initiatives

- Develop and maintain comprehensive knowledge of industry trends, emerging technologies, and best practices and apply technical fluency in relevant platforms and approved tools to provide strategic guidance and innovative solutions for complex projects

- Promotes reuse-first, AI-assisted practices for analysis and documentation across the team, ensuring human review and alignment to delivery standards.

- Evaluate public cloud business opportunities, collaborating with internal teams to align financial strategies with organizational goals.

- Manage and execute standard monthly billing processes for public cloud providers, ensuring accuracy and compliance.

- Interpret financial data to understand changes in cloud spend, providing insights into the “hows” and “whys” of month-over-month variations.

- Collaborate with cross-functional teams to drive data-informed decision-making and support key business initiatives.

- Strong track record of leading through change, navigating ambiguous situations, and managing dependencies in complex projects

- Strong proficiency in Excel and data analysis, with the ability to handle large datasets and complex calculations.

- Knowledge of public cloud providers (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud) and cloud cost management tools.

- Ability to interpret and analyze financial data, providing strategic insights and recommendations.

- Excellent communication skills, with the ability to convey complex financial information to diverse audiences.

Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills

- FinOps certification and AWS Cloud Practitioner certification (or equivalent for Azure/Google) highly desirable.

- Strong understanding of cloud billing processes, financial reporting, and experience with cloud cost management platforms and tools.

- Proven ability to work collaboratively in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

- Demonstrated ability to lead through change and manage ambiguity effectively.


Own public cloud billing and contract operations; drive FinOps savings through advanced analytics and data-driven insights.

jobs.title: Design Operations Manager
jobs.description:
As the Design Operations Manager, Senior Associate within Digital, you will be responsible for planning and managing the day-to-day workflow and processes and reporting that support our growing digital design project work across Digital Customer Experience (DCE).  You will lead delivery for complex programs and enable the design organization to operate efficiently and predictably. You will partner closely with design leads, product, technology, and finance/business management to align resources with strategic priorities, strengthen governance, and increase delivery transparency. In this role, you will enhance ways of working across teams by scaling effective practices, managing risks, and promoting adoption of tools and approaches (including AI and automation) that improve both quality and speed of delivery . - Partner with Digital Design, Product, and Line-of-Business partners to translate demand into capacity and resourcing plans; verify deliverables and handoffs are clearly defined and agreed across stakeholders and internal teams

- Collaborate with Design Leads, Product Owners, Tech Leads, and Scrum Masters to guide end-to-end execution and delivery, strengthening concept readiness and artifact quality

- Consult with teams on planning design work (size, scope, sequence, next steps) so that teams understand requirements and rationale

- Track delivery across projects (small to large), serving as the single point of contact for project status & issue management to ensure milestones, status, decisions, and risks are consistently documented, communicated, and reported as needed

- Leverage traditional and AI tooling to develop on rhythms, activities, and ceremonies to improve predictability and reduce rework

- Uphold company standards and best practices and champion continuous process improvements to drive craft and design output

- Develop and maintain reusable documentation (SOPs, templates, playbooks) and support engagement/communication to sustain team health

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills:

- 4+ years of project/ program management or design operations experience working with digital UX design teams

- Strong understanding of the product development lifecycle at scale; fluent in Agile and Waterfall delivery methodologies

- Proficient with delivery/ops tooling (e.g., Atlassian/Jira, Monday.com) and using it to drive workflow transparency and reporting

- Excellent communication skills: synthesize delivery status into clear narratives and dashboards with appropriate rigor, discretion, implications, and recommended actions

- Demonstrated ability to build plans, prioritize work, and drive execution across multiple concurrent workstreams

- Strong problem-solving skills: able to structure ambiguous situations, identify root causes, and translate insights into pragmatic solutions and recommendations

- Highly organized and proactive; able to operate independently while coordinating cross-functional teams in a fast-paced, distributed environment

- Proven cross-functional collaborator with the ability to influence outcomes without direct authority; strong active listening, stakeholder management, and sound judgment

- Adaptable and comfortable navigating change, ambiguity, and evolving priorities; passionate about customer-centric design and continuous professional growth

- Systems-minded and improvement-oriented: identifies patterns and root causes, and implements sustainable process/operating improvements

- Familiarity with design and AI-assisted tools (e.g., Figma, GitHub Copilot) and the aptitude to evaluate and integrate emerging tools

Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills

- Experience working with and/or supporting design systems

- Knowledge of current design industry trends and evolving best practices

- Strong facilitation skills, including workshops, decisioning, and alignment forums

- Comfortable leveraging AI tooling to improve operational efficiency, decision support, documentation, and communication (in alignment with firm policies)


The Design Manager will be responsible for planning and managing the day-to-day workflow and processes and reporting that support our growing digital design project work across Digital Customer Experience (DCE).

jobs.title: Branch Operations Lead - Leesburg - Leesburg, VA
jobs.description:
At Chase, we are passionate about creating memorable experiences for our clients and employees, making them feel welcomed, valued, and understood. We build lasting relationships by doing the right thing, exceeding expectations, and embracing diversity and inclusion.

As a Branch Operations Lead in a Chase Branch, you'll be at the heart of our branch operations, working closely with the Branch Manager, branch employees, and our team of experts. Your role is crucial in ensuring that our clients' financial transactions are handled with precision and care, all while adhering to our policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements.

A typical day will involve assisting clients with their transactions, but it doesn't stop there. You'll have the opportunity to make a real difference by introducing clients to self-service options that simplify their banking experience and by building lasting relationships with them. Throughout the week, you'll also dedicate time to reviewing branch operations and keeping the branch team informed about the latest policies and procedures. Your leadership will ensure that our branch not only meets but exceeds control expectations, setting a positive tone for everyone who walks through our doors.

Job responsibilities

- Collaborate with the Branch Manager to create a welcoming and vibrant atmosphere in the branch, ensuring every client enjoys an exceptional experience and feels part of a dynamic community.

- Greet clients warmly as they enter the branch, making them feel valued and appreciated. Demonstrate genuine care and concern during interactions, assisting with transactions, managing lobby flow, and scheduling meetings to build trusted relationships.

- Engage clients with clear, polite communication to understand and help them effectively. Anticipate their needs while checking them into the waiting queue, ensuring a smooth visit.

- Lead branch operations, including managing cash devices like the cash vault and ATM. Resolve any client issues quickly and effectively, paying attention to detail and striving for consistency while adhering to all bank policies and procedures.

- Introduce clients to our friendly branch team, who collaborate to deliver seamless service with care and sincerity. Work together to build lasting relationships and assist with any specialized financial needs, elevating the client experience.

- Simplify clients' banking experience by sharing self-service options, allowing them to access their accounts anytime, day or night.

- Work closely with the Branch Manager to support all aspects of branch operations, including maintaining high standards for loss control, compliance, and audits, ensuring the branch operates smoothly and securely.

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills

- You take pride in adhering to policies, procedures, and regulatory banking requirements, ensuring everything runs smoothly and efficiently.

- You are committed to maintaining a keen eye for detail and staying organized, which helps you juggle multiple tasks effectively.

- You are proud of your leadership skills and operational proficiency, ensuring transaction accuracy while thriving in a collaborative team environment.

- You have a strong passion for educating the branch team and partners, helping them stay connected and informed.

- You excel at building meaningful connections and engaging with clients, always ready to educate them and refer them to our team of experts when needed.

- You have 1+ years of retail banking experience.

- You have a high school degree, GED, or foreign equivalent.

- You have the ability to work branch hours including weekends and evenings.

Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills

- You have 6+ months of Associate Banker (Teller) experience.

- You have a college degree or military equivalent.

Training and Travel Requirement

- You’ll successfully complete our Branch Operations Lead Training Program before being considered for placement as a Branch Operations Lead.

- You’ll need to be able to travel as required for in-person training and meetings.


Deliver exceptional client experience as a Branch Operations Lead, embodying our commitment to hospitality and client care.

jobs.title: Amenity Services- 383 General Manager
jobs.description:
JPMorgan Chase is seeking an experienced hospitality professional to fill the role of Amenity Services General Manager at our newly renovated midtown building, 383 Madison Avenue, New York City. The role involves overseeing operations for Client Conferencing, Multi Concept Food Hall, Branded Coffee Bars, Catering and Lobby Reception teams, similar to a large hotel's guest services. The successful candidate will interface with internal and external partners, manage complex budgets, and promote program innovation in food, menu service and technology. This role is a unique opportunity to create and execute strategic initiatives for Amenity Service in our new headquarters, ensuring efficient and customer-focused management.

As a General Manager of Amenity Services within JPMorgan Chase's new 383 Madison Avenue, you will be responsible for creating an exceptional experience for our employees and clients. Your role will encompass the oversight of operations for Client Conferencing, Multi Concept Food Hall, Branded Coffee Bars, Catering, and Lobby Reception teams, ensuring efficient and customer-focused management. You will be tasked with strategic planning, budget management, fostering a positive work environment, and promoting innovation in our amenity services. This role offers a unique opportunity to shape the amenity services of a large, dynamic organization and make a significant impact on the daily experiences of thousands of employees and visitors.

Job Responsibilities:

- Develop and maintain positive relationships with the other departments within the building. Liaise with business leaders to ensure they are engaged in employees and client facing strategies

- Manage the foodservice vendor to provide a best-in-class unique food and beverage experience for our clients and employees

- Act as the primary point of contact for addressing inquiries and issues related to Amenity Services

- Foster a sense of community among all aspect of Amenity Services and other departments within 383 Madison

jobs.title: Program Management Banking Book – Product Owner – Vice President
jobs.description:

jobs.title: Chase Home Lending Vice President, Program Management – Correspondent Channel Programs
jobs.description:
Join our fun, high-energy Correspondent team as a Program Manager in Chase Home Lending, where you’ll apply your strong understanding of home lending products while serving as a key point of contact for correspondent clients.  Our Chase Correspondent Home Lending Team purchases closed mortgage loans and mortgage servicing rights from independent mortgage banks and financial institutions across the country with a focus on delivering liquidity, reliability and market leading services.  We’re a relationship-driven investor committed to our clients and the communities we serve together. With Chase, clients get unparalleled access to the full capabilities of JPMorgan Chase — extending far beyond the services of a traditional correspondent investor.

As the Vice President of Program Management in Correspondent Channel Programs, you will lead complex, cross-functional business programs within the Correspondent Channel of Home Lending, with an emphasis on Non-Agency, Government (FHA & VA), and Builder programs and the delivery of enterprise-wide initiatives that improve market share, execution, controls, scalability, and partner outcomes.

This role requires an experienced program leader with strong governance discipline, the ability to influence across functions without direct authority, and a proven track record delivering multiple workstreams concurrently in a highly controlled environment.

Job Responsibilities:

- Assist in driving the business development strategy to support the growth of the correspondent initiatives

- Responsible for Agency relations associated with the Correspondent programs and partner with Client Management team to build and cultivate a strong pipeline of approved clients for the programs

- Field questions from the Client Management team and all stakeholders on specifics of transaction structure, delivery methods and current policies

- Partner with Client Management team as subject matter expert in explaining program parameters to the client and delivering comprehensive options and solutions tailored to the needs of the client

- Ensure all transactions are executed in accordance with policies, procedures and controls

- Collaborate with risk and legal in drafting, review, negotiation and execution of all supporting legal agreements related to the programs

- Establish client implementation schedule and responsible for all related tracking, reporting and internal and external communications

- Partner with Transformation, technology and business stakeholders to ensure execution and ongoing success of short and long term channel objectives

- Monitor program deliveries and responsible for identifying potential issues/risks and provide recommendations for the resolution of all program risk events

-
Perform Internal Partnership Management, including regularly occurring meetings with key stakeholders in correspondent, agency relations, servicing, credit risk and capital markets

Required Qualifications, Capabilities, and Skills

- Five years of Mortgage business/industry knowledge required, especially the Correspondent business

- Bachelor's Degree

- Extensive experience with Microsoft Excel, Word, Pitch Pro and PowerPoint

- Outstanding verbal and written communication skills

- Strong problem solving, negotiation and analytical skills

- Proven partnership experience in working across various departments and lines of business

- Exposure to Mortgage Finance including Pricing, Secondary Marketing operations, mortgage servicing and file delivery requirements. Understanding of agency deal structures and legal documentation

- Proven track record of drafting and reviewing complex legal agreements as well as end to end ownership of various types of servicing acquisition programs


Ensure execution of programs with Chase approved clients to achieve the Correspondent business strategic goals.

jobs.title: Amenity Services Program Manager - Vice President
jobs.description:
As an Amenity Services Program Manager in Amenity Services at JPMorgan Chase’s global headquarters at 270 Park Avenue in New York City, you will play a pivotal role in an operational, world-class facility featuring iconic architecture and best-in-class client and amenity spaces. Amenity Services encompasses four core functions: Lobby Reception, Employee Dining, Conference Center, and Client Center. In this role, you will support business case development, capital projects, and data and analytics initiatives across all amenity functions. The ideal candidate is a strategic leader with a robust background in hospitality operations, vendor management, and data-driven performance reporting. You will be responsible for synthesizing operational data into actionable insights, driving cross-functional collaboration, and supporting management with key business metrics to inform decision-making and operational improvements. This position reports directly to the Amenity Services General Manager and partners closely with Vendor Partners, Amenity Services Leaders, Technology, Global Real Estate, and other corporate stakeholders.

Join a dynamic team at the heart of JPMorgan Chase’s flagship location, where innovation meets excellence in client and employee experience. As the Amenity Services Program Manager Vice President, you will be empowered to shape the future of hospitality operations in a premier environment, leveraging cutting-edge analytics and strategic partnerships to deliver world-class service. This is an opportunity to lead with impact—driving operational excellence, influencing capital projects, and collaborating with top-tier professionals across the organization. If you are passionate about elevating standards, optimizing performance, and creating memorable experiences, this role offers a platform to showcase your expertise and contribute to the continued success of a global leader in financial services.

Job responsibilities

- Strategically lead the creation of data-driven business cases and executive presentations to inform major decisions and capital projects, synthesizing operational data and trends into actionable insights for leadership.

- Consistently establish and maintain recurring reporting cadences and dashboards, ensuring timely visibility into key business metrics and delivering clear, executive-ready recommendations that support strategic and operational improvements.

- Comprehensively own all data and reporting for 270 Park amenity functions, including room utilization, POS sales, lobby traffic, and vendor performance, translating operational data into clear narratives and presentations for senior forums.

- Proactively identify risks and provide actionable options with financial impact assessments, structuring complex building-wide challenges such as space utilization and service model changes into clear recommendations and executable plans.

- Diligently maintain accountability for all vendor deliverables, ensuring data accuracy, SLA adherence, and prompt resolution of operational gaps.

- Promptly escalate issues with data-driven evidence and monitor performance to ensure compliance and operational excellence.

- Collaboratively serve as the primary liaison between vendor partners and internal customers, resolving issues and ensuring KPIs are met.

- Effectively manage budgets within a complex financial structure while driving innovation in food, menu, and technology.

- Regularly review and analyze operational data to flag bottlenecks and propose process improvements with hiring managers and stakeholders.

- Accurately align expectations and close with clarity on total compensation philosophy when advising on offers and business cases.

- Continuously partner with Amenity Services Leaders, Technology, Global Real Estate, and other corporate stakeholders to refine reporting, analytics, and operational strategies.

Required qualifications, capabilities and skills

- Strong client focus, business management, and communication skills.

- Demonstrated ability to write business cases and executive presentations.

- Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (PowerPoint, Excel, Word).

- Experience managing vendor teams and multi-unit operations.

- 7+ Years of combined experience in strategy, transformation, or business case development, with direct exposure to real estate, hospitality, or amenity operations at scale.

- Experience developing long-term strategies, managing projects, and integrating technology such as digital tools, mobile ordering, self-service kiosks, and contactless payment systems.

- Highly organized, detail-oriented, and able to manage multiple priorities and budgets.

- Strong interpersonal, relationship-building, crisis management, and problem-solving skills.

- Proven ability to structure ambiguous problems and deliver executive-ready recommendations under tight timelines.

- Comfortable operating in a fast-paced, in-person, high-visibility corporate headquarters environment.

Preferred qualifications, capabilities and skills

- Bachelor’s degree preferred.

- Advanced Excel and PowerPoint skills; experience with Event Management Systems EMS or equivalent data platforms is a strong plus.

- Minimum ten years of relevant foodservice experience restaurant or business environment; financial institution background a plus


Lead amenity services strategy, analytics, and vendor management at JPMorgan Chase’s flagship headquarters, driving excellence.

jobs.title: Compliance - Digital Asset Intelligence Operations Manager – Vice President
jobs.description:
Bring your Expertise to JPMorgan Chase.  As part of Risk Management and Compliance, you are at the center of keeping JPMorgan Chase strong and resilient. You help the firm grow its business in a responsible way by anticipating new and emerging risks, and using your expert judgement to solve real-world challenges that impact our company, customers and communities. Our culture in Risk Management and Compliance is all about thinking outside the box, challenging the status quo and striving to be best-in-class.

As a Vice President in Global Financial Crimes Compliance - Digital Asset Intelligence Operations, you will lead a high-performing team responsible for detecting, investigating, and mitigating money laundering and terrorist financing (ML/TF) risks across both fiat and digital assets. Additionally, you will collaborate with partners across Risk, Operations, Technology, and Legal to design innovative detection approaches and deliver impactful intelligence with a special focus on blockchain-based products, platforms, and customer and entity types across global markets. You help us strengthen our controls, inform strategy, and share appropriate insights while fostering an inclusive, growth-oriented team culture.

Job responsibilities

- Coach, train, and upskill the team on current and emerging risk typologies, including digital asset typologies; lead workshops to drive awareness of on-chain risks and investigative best practices.

- Produce and maintain reporting that monitors key trends (on-chain and off-chain), articulates risk drivers, and recommends risk-mitigating actions to leadership.

- Partner with data analysts and technology teams to design typologies and help build monitoring/detection tools for fiat and digital assets, including on-chain tracing, clustering, wallet/VASP screening, and cross-chain analytics.

- Identify and acquire relevant customer, transaction, exchange/VASP, and on-chain data across platforms to assess suspicious and high-risk activity; ensure appropriate data governance and controls.

- Lead and conduct complex investigations employing blockchain analytics and forensic tools (e.g., Chainalysis Reactor, Elliptic, TRM Labs) alongside traditional AML platforms; resolve cases and escalate significant matters.

- Drive process improvements and efficiencies that anticipate stakeholder needs and scale globally (case triage, risk-based prioritization, alert tuning, and typology iteration for digital assets and fiat).

- Coordinate investigative activities within GFCC and across lines of business, regions, and functions; present intelligence findings and recommendations to senior stakeholders, Legal, Audit, and Risk.

- Share appropriate information with external law enforcement in alignment with policy and legal requirements; support responses to regulatory inquiries and exams.

- Collaborate with Anti-Money Laundering Investigations and senior stakeholders to enhance detection and reporting outcomes across digital assets and traditional payment rails.

- Ensure accurate and timely preparation and filing of Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) in accordance with FinCEN, BSA/AML, and sanctions standards.

- Independently manage the team’s case inventory, set priorities, and allocate resources to meet departmental objectives and service-level expectations.

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills

- 5 years of financial crime investigations experience, including SAR preparation and filing; at least 3 years focused on digital asset investigations or compliance.

- Demonstrated people leadership and team development experience, including coaching investigators and enhancing capabilities.

- Proven project management experience delivering defined outcomes (process scaling, typology launches, alert optimization).

- Expert knowledge of banking systems and AML typologies, with specialization in digital asset typologies and cryptocurrency trends.

- Proficiency with BSA/AML and sanctions regulatory requirements (including OFAC) and familiarity with FinCEN guidance relevant to digital assets.

- Must have hands-on experience using Chainalysis reactor to trace and assess suspicious activity; experience with digital asset transaction monitoring and wallet/VASP screening.

- Experience acquiring and analyzing customer and transaction data across multiple systems, including exchange/VASP data and on-chain sources; ability to synthesize complex findings into clear, actionable recommendations.

- Strong collaboration skills with partners across businesses, regions, and functions; confident presenter to senior audiences.

- Excellent written and verbal communication tailored to technical and non-technical stakeholders; high attention to detail, sound judgment, and commitment to ethical decision-making.

- Ability to operate amid ambiguity, prioritize multiple tasks, and manage case queues to meet objectives.

Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills

- Breadth across typologies including terrorist financing, fraud, human trafficking/smuggling, transnational criminal organizations, corruption, cybercrime, proliferation financing, internal risk and sanctions, wildlife trafficking, and cyber-enabled laundering.

- Familiarity with tokenization, DeFi protocols and platforms, stablecoins, smart contracts, cross-chain activity, and other emerging digital asset technologies.

- Prior collaboration with law enforcement, regulatory counterparts, or industry consortia on digital asset investigations.

- Professional certifications: CAMS, CFE, CFCS; and digital asset certifications (e.g., Certified Blockchain Expert) or platform certifications (e.g., Chainalysis, TRM Labs, Elliptic).

- Proficiency with AML software and transaction monitoring platforms (e.g., Actimize, Mantas).

- Experience engaging global stakeholders and navigating complex, matrixed organizations; change management experience in scaling processes, controls, or investigative programs.

- Familiarity with emerging financial crime trends and digital asset products (e.g., digital tokens and tokenized assets), including typologies such as trade-based money laundering and cyber-enabled laundering.


Direct a top team to detect, investigate, and reduce money laundering and terrorist financing risks across fiat and digital assets.

jobs.title: Lead Site Reliability Engineer - Public Cloud Operational Excellence
jobs.description:
As a Lead Site Reliability Engineer at JPMorgan Chase within the Public Cloud team, you will blend hands-on engineering with program leadership to promote platform stability, ensure consistent execution across SRE teams, and partner closely with Engineering and Product to deliver measurable improvements in availability, support outcomes, and cost of failure.
Job Responsibilities

- Drive consistency across SRE teams: establish and scale a “gold standard” for SLOs, on-call readiness, runbooks, postmortems, action tracking, and operational readiness across AWS/Azure/GCP.

- Partner with Engineering and Product: embed reliability outcomes into roadmaps and delivery plans; convert incidents, support signals, and error budget trends into prioritized backlog with measurable impact.

- Operational excellence & BPMs: design and run operating cadences (incident/stability reviews, KPI reviews, planning inputs), standardize intake/prioritization, and ensure closed-loop execution.

- Risk governance: align reliability operations to risk/control expectations; operationalize recurring remediations (e.g., configuration drift, repeat findings) through centralized automation without sacrificing velocity.

- Ticket reduction & automation opportunities: identify top drivers of support load and operational toil; build and maintain an automation opportunity pipeline; track adoption and deflection.

- Platform stability metrics: own cross-platform reporting (SLO attainment, incident trends, MTTR/MTTI, change failure rate, ticket deflection, customer impact/cost of failure).

- AI for reliability operations: apply AI/LLMs to improve triage, incident summarization, correlation/symptom mapping, and guardrailed automation; measure accuracy, safety, and outcomes.

- Hands-on leadership: stay close to designs and critical implementations; lead systemic remediation and major incident response improvements.

Required qualifications, skills, and capabilities

-  5+ years in SRE / production engineering / platform reliability / infrastructure operations at enterprise scale

- Demonstrated success driving cross-team standardization and measurable reliability outcomes through influence and operating mechanisms.

- Deep knowledge of SLOs/SLIs, error budgets, observability, incident response, postmortems, and change reliability.

- Strong experience partnering with Engineering and Product leadership to align priorities and deliver results.

- Hands-on experience with AWS and/or Azure  and automation/IaC fundamentals (e.g., Python/Go/Bash, Terraform, CI/CD).

- Experience using AI/LLM-enabled approaches in operations (AIOps, AI-assisted troubleshooting, agentic workflows) with appropriate controls and measurement.

Preferred Qualifications

- Improved SLO attainment and reduced Sev1/Sev2 frequency; fewer repeat incidents.

- Reduced MTTR/MTTI and lower change failure rate; reduced customer minutes impacted (cost of failure).

- Measurable ticket reduction/deflection via scaled automation and self-service adoption.

- Consistent operating model adopted across SRE teams with trusted executive reporting.


Lead and conduct resiliency design reviews, break up complex problems, and act as a technical lead for medium to large sized products

jobs.title: Branch Operations Lead - Bethlehem Fairview Ave (New Build) - Bethlehem, PA
jobs.description:
At Chase, we are passionate about creating memorable experiences for our clients and employees, making them feel welcomed, valued, and understood. We build lasting relationships by doing the right thing, exceeding expectations, and embracing diversity and inclusion.

As a Branch Operations Lead in a Chase Branch, you'll be at the heart of our branch operations, working closely with the Branch Manager, branch employees, and our team of experts. Your role is crucial in ensuring that our clients' financial transactions are handled with precision and care, all while adhering to our policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements.

A typical day will involve assisting clients with their transactions, but it doesn't stop there. You'll have the opportunity to make a real difference by introducing clients to self-service options that simplify their banking experience and by building lasting relationships with them. Throughout the week, you'll also dedicate time to reviewing branch operations and keeping the branch team informed about the latest policies and procedures. Your leadership will ensure that our branch not only meets but exceeds control expectations, setting a positive tone for everyone who walks through our doors.

Job responsibilities

- Collaborate with the Branch Manager to create a welcoming and vibrant atmosphere in the branch, ensuring every client enjoys an exceptional experience and feels part of a dynamic community.

- Greet clients warmly as they enter the branch, making them feel valued and appreciated. Demonstrate genuine care and concern during interactions, assisting with transactions, managing lobby flow, and scheduling meetings to build trusted relationships.

- Engage clients with clear, polite communication to understand and help them effectively. Anticipate their needs while checking them into the waiting queue, ensuring a smooth visit.

- Lead branch operations, including managing cash devices like the cash vault and ATM. Resolve any client issues quickly and effectively, paying attention to detail and striving for consistency while adhering to all bank policies and procedures.

- Introduce clients to our friendly branch team, who collaborate to deliver seamless service with care and sincerity. Work together to build lasting relationships and assist with any specialized financial needs, elevating the client experience.

- Simplify clients' banking experience by sharing self-service options, allowing them to access their accounts anytime, day or night.

- Work closely with the Branch Manager to support all aspects of branch operations, including maintaining high standards for loss control, compliance, and audits, ensuring the branch operates smoothly and securely.

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills

- You take pride in adhering to policies, procedures, and regulatory banking requirements, ensuring everything runs smoothly and efficiently.

- You are committed to maintaining a keen eye for detail and staying organized, which helps you juggle multiple tasks effectively.

- You are proud of your leadership skills and operational proficiency, ensuring transaction accuracy while thriving in a collaborative team environment.

- You have a strong passion for educating the branch team and partners, helping them stay connected and informed.

- You excel at building meaningful connections and engaging with clients, always ready to educate them and refer them to our team of experts when needed.

- You have 1+ years of retail banking experience.

- You have a high school degree, GED, or foreign equivalent.

- You have the ability to work branch hours including weekends and evenings.

Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills

- You have 6+ months of Associate Banker (Teller) experience.

- You have a college degree or military equivalent.

Training and Travel Requirement

- You’ll successfully complete our Branch Operations Lead Training Program before being considered for placement as a Branch Operations Lead.

- You’ll need to be able to travel as required for in-person training and meetings.


Deliver exceptional client experience as a Branch Operations Lead, embodying our commitment to hospitality and client care.
